doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Ballads, Skylark and piano harmony
summary: They discuss pacing a set, Skylark and True Love, and Ross's use of the middle of the keyboard.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And it just seems to be a relief sometimes to just calm down for a moment. That’s what I think anyway. And Tommy played “Skylark” too which is a—
Yeah, I played a slow one too, and I guess many of us did. But what we try to do is alternate so we don’t get too many of the same thing in a row.
It was a nice paced set and it was nice to hear “Skylark” which isn’t something that someone always does. And you were playing “True Love?”
Yes I was. [inaudible] medley and went into three quarter time.
I think you found the lost chord too.
I mean one thing about jazz piano is the kind of instant harmonization, what can you do with that, and that was some really interesting things there.
Well, if you enjoyed it, I’m happy.

I loved it. And you seem to favor the middle of the keyboard a great deal, and I kept waiting for you to finally get up there, and when you did it was such a nice, really a nice release kind of I guess.
Well I’m a lazy guy. And I’m disinclined to reach too far in either direction.
